narration.label: M01: "Accounts payable · a payment run" river
narration.text: Every week, accounts payable sends money out to hundreds of vendors, and almost all of it lands exactly where it should.

narration.label: R01: The Booz Allen letter
narration.text: Then an email like this shows up. Booz Allen, apparently, with new bank details, {{days_before_payment_words}} days before we owe them {{exposure_millions}} million dollars.

narration.label: M02: Three stat cards; each card must appear as its sentence starts (use word timings)
narration.text: This really happens. In 2018, twenty-three and a half million dollars was diverted from a government payment system this way. Last year the FBI counted three billion lost to email fraud. And the fix everyone agrees on is simple: call back on a number you already trust.

narration.label: M03: Sources merging into vendor360
narration.text: The hard part is finding that number. It's spread across four systems. So Probity uses Zetaris to join our vendor master with live USAspending and SEC EDGAR records, in one semantic layer.

narration.label: M04: "Stopped before the money moves."
narration.text: For this letter, the answer is clear: stop the payment before the money moves.

narration.label: R02: Hold banner, then the sweep banner
narration.text: It holds the payment, hands us a safe number to call, and checks the rest of Friday's run while it's at it.

narration.label: M05: The four agent cards (each card highlights as it is named)
narration.text: Under the hood, there are four agents. The Letter Reader uses Nemotron Ultra to read the letter twice, and both readings have to agree. The Registry Scout runs the Zetaris checks. The Identity Examiner double-checks the evidence. And the Gate Officer, which is plain code, makes the call.

narration.label: R03: Trace rail, agents handing off
narration.text: You can watch them hand the case to each other, step by step, right here in the trace.

narration.label: R04: S10 injection: hidden-instruction card, page bands, HOLD
narration.text: Now here's a sneaky one. This letter hides a message telling the AI to approve it. Probity doesn't obey. It quotes the hidden text as evidence, and holds the payment.

narration.label: R05: The live S1 run (sped-up wait, then the decision). "Decision: hold" must be spoken exactly as the HOLD reveal appears
narration.text: So let's run the Booz Allen request for real. The Reader pulls out every claim, including a line asking us not to use the old phone number. The Scout checks our vendor master and the public registries through Zetaris. The new address doesn't match anything we know, so the Examiner sends the Scout back to dig. It walks Booz Allen's corporate family, forty-one companies, and finds it. The address is real, but it belongs to a different Booz Allen company that has never billed us. Decision: hold. The number to call comes from SEC filings, and the one in the letter goes on the do-not-use list.

narration.label: R06: S2 two same-name companies, two scripts
narration.text: Here, two companies share the same name. Probity won't guess which one sent it. It writes a call-back script for each.

narration.label: R07: Memory hold (L3Harris, R5 chip)
narration.text: It remembers, too. A bank account caught in an earlier scam turns up on a new L3Harris request, so that one's held as well.

narration.label: R14: As-of scrubber back to "Request received"
narration.text: And you can rewind. This is what Probity knew when the letter arrived: the New Jersey company wasn't in the picture yet.

narration.label: M06: Lineage chain
narration.text: Every fact in that decision came from Zetaris, and each one traces back to the exact rows behind it.

narration.label: R09: Evidence drawer lineage, then Re-run in Zetaris
narration.text: Click any fact to see its source, its table and its query. Hit re-run, and Zetaris confirms the rows still match.

narration.label: R10: Zetaris console: RUN DQ result
narration.text: And the payment-run sweep is a real Zetaris data-quality rule, running right inside Zetaris.

narration.label: M07: Nightshift receipt
narration.text: Every model call goes through Meterless Nightshift to a pinned Nemotron model.

narration.label: R13: Sweep panel, DQ7 hit
narration.text: Nobody asked, but it checked anyway, and found two vendors sharing one bank account.

narration.label: M08: Hold list in dollars, median per check
narration.text: That's {{sweep_count_words}} more payments flagged, and the controller gets a hold list in dollars.

narration.label: M09: End card with build credit
narration.text: Probity never moves money. It just makes sure it goes to the right place. Grok built the Zetaris data layer and the tests; Claude Code built the agents and the interface.
